themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Queens Village experienced a spike in street sign complaints THIS WEEK—6 missing signs (586% above 8-week average of 0.9) and 10 dangling signs last week (344% above average of 2.2)—suggesting rapid deterioration of traffic/directional infrastructure that could create safety and navigation hazards.
evidence: 6 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.53)
10 dangling street sign complaints last week vs. 2.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.97)
Combined 16 complaints in 2 weeks suggests pattern, not random failure
reporting_angles: Inspect specific intersections with highest complaint density; document safety risks (visibility, traffic flow)
Interview DOT about maintenance schedule and resource allocation for Queens Village vs. other districts

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 6 last week—a 1500% surge above the 8-week average of 0.4 complaints per week (z-score: 11.62)—indicating either a sudden enforcement crackdown, organized poster activity, or previously unreported problem surfacing in residents' complaints.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 11.62, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
1500% percentage increase; highest severity rating among all spikes
Baseline so low (0.4/week) that even small absolute number registers as extreme statistical deviation
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify if posting is concentrated around specific corridors or transit hubs
Contact DSNY about whether increased 311 reporting reflects actual activity or improved complaint awareness

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints hit 12 THIS WEEK, a 773% jump above the 8-week average of 1.4 complaints (z-score: 7.54), suggesting rapid degradation of street infrastructure that could indicate broader pavement failure or water damage across the district.
evidence: 12 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.54)
Aligns with recurring community board budget request for street reconstruction (filed [01] times year-over-year)
reporting_angles: Ground truth: photograph curb damage in areas with highest complaint density; assess whether hazard affects pedestrians/wheelchairs
Interview DOT about backlog of curb repairs and whether weather events (snow/ice category had 1197 complaints) may have accelerated damage

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 5 last week—567% above the 8-week average of 0.8 (z-score: 6.43)—suggesting either a localized pack problem, seasonal behavioral change, or enforcement gaps in parks/open spaces where community board repeatedly requests better amenity maintenance.
evidence: 5 unleashed dog complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.43)
Converges with recurring CB budget request for park maintenance and new/expanded amenities, suggesting parks may be focal point
reporting_angles: Interview residents at parks/playgrounds about safety perception and whether unleashed dogs pose threat to children
Contact NYPD and Parks Enforcement about off-leash dog enforcement presence and whether officers are responding to complaints

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping Enforcement Wave
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints reached 4 THIS WEEK—a 540% spike above the 8-week average of 0.6 (z-score: 4.85)—possibly reflecting heightened resident awareness, enforcement efforts around schools, or outdoor venue violations in a health-sensitive context.
evidence: 4 smoking/vaping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.85)
No prior media coverage or CB discussion of smoking enforcement in this district
reporting_angles: Identify where complaints are clustered—near schools, parks, or transit hubs—to assess if violations target youth
Contact DOHMH about any recent education campaigns or enforcement operations in Queens Village
